#** Set up Phase Diff **
```{r}
# Swap PPhase and TPhase for RR and SBT
StatBoth <- Stat %>%
  filter(week == "Both") %>%
  mutate(
    PPhase_temp = ifelse(Bio %in% c("RR", "SBT"), TPhase, PPhase),
    TPhase_temp = ifelse(Bio %in% c("RR", "SBT"), PPhase, TPhase),
    PPhase = PPhase_temp,
    TPhase = TPhase_temp
    ) %>%
  select(PPhase, TPhase, Patient, Bio, age) %>%
    mutate(
    PPhase = as.numeric(PPhase),
    TPhase = as.numeric(TPhase)
    )


# Function to compute signed circular phase difference
circular_diff_signed <- function(a, b) {
  diff1 <- a - b
  diff2 <- (a - b) - 24 * sign(a - b)  # Adjust for wrap-around
  ifelse(abs(diff1) < abs(diff2), diff1, diff2)  # Choose the shorter signed difference
}

# Compute mean phase difference for each patient
pairwise_differences <- StatBoth %>%
  group_by(Patient, age) %>%
  summarise(
    PPhaseDiff = mean(combn(PPhase, 2, function(x) circular_diff_signed(x[1], x[2]), simplify = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE),
    TPhaseDiff = mean(combn(TPhase, 2, function(x) circular_diff_signed(x[1], x[2]), simplify = TRUE), na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# Generate all unique biometric pairs
biometric_pairs <- combn(unique(StatBoth$Bio), 2, simplify = FALSE)

# Compute pairwise differences for each biometric pair
for (pair in biometric_pairs) {
  bio1 <- pair[1]
  bio2 <- pair[2]
  column_name_PPhase <- paste0(bio1, "_vs_", bio2, "_PPhase")
  column_name_TPhase <- paste0(bio1, "_vs_", bio2, "_TPhase")
  
  # Summarise to ensure only one value per Patient-Bio before pivot_wider()
  pairwise_values <- StatBoth %>%
    filter(Bio %in% pair) %>%
    group_by(Patient, age, Bio) %>%
    summarise(PPhase = mean(PPhase, na.rm = TRUE), 
              TPhase = mean(TPhase, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
    pivot_wider(names_from = Bio, values_from = c(PPhase, TPhase)) %>%
    mutate(
      across(starts_with("PPhase_"), ~ as.numeric(unlist(.))),  # Ensure numeric conversion
      across(starts_with("TPhase_"), ~ as.numeric(unlist(.))),
      !!column_name_PPhase := circular_diff_signed(!!sym(paste0("PPhase_", bio1)), !!sym(paste0("PPhase_", bio2))),
      !!column_name_TPhase := circular_diff_signed(!!sym(paste0("TPhase_", bio1)), !!sym(paste0("TPhase_", bio2)))
    ) %>%
    select(Patient, !!column_name_PPhase, !!column_name_TPhase)

  # Merge results into main dataframe
  pairwise_differences <- left_join(pairwise_differences, pairwise_values, by = "Patient")
}

# Reorder columns: PPhase first, then TPhase
pairwise_differences <- pairwise_differences %>%
  select(
    Patient, PPhaseDiff, TPhaseDiff, 
    matches("_PPhase$"),  # All PPhase pairwise columns
    matches("_TPhase$")   # All TPhase pairwise columns
  )

PhaseDiff <- pairwise_differences

 #** Export the data *
    export_path <- paste0(valid_path, "/Stats/Phase Diff.xlsx")
    write.xlsx(PhaseDiff, export_path, rowNames = FALSE, firstRow = TRUE)
        
# Clean up
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), CoreDatasets))   
```

#** Relationship Analysis: Core Functions **#
```{r}
# --- Define the outcome metrics (Y variables)
outcome_metrics <- c("Amplitude","Mesor","PPhase","TPhase","Max","Min")

# --- Define the predictor metrics (X variables)
predictor_metrics <- c("age","gender","BMI")

# Combine all unique combinations of predictor and outcome variables
regression_combinations <- expand_grid(
  Predictor = predictor_metrics,
  Outcome = outcome_metrics
)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# --- NEW FUNCTION: Run GLM (Linear Terms Only) ---
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
run_glm_regression <- function(data, predictor, outcome) {
  
  results <- list(
    Linear_Coefficient = NA,
    Linear_P_Value = NA,
    Quadratic_Coefficient = NA, 
    Quadratic_P_Value = NA,     
    R_Squared = NA
  )
  
  model_family <- gaussian(link = "identity")
  
  if (predictor == "gender") {
    formula_str <- paste(outcome, "~", predictor)
    model <- glm(as.formula(formula_str), data = data, family = model_family)
    model_summary <- summary(model)
    
    results$R_Squared = 1 - (model$deviance / model$null.deviance)
    
    gender_term_name <- grep(paste0("^", predictor), rownames(model_summary$coefficients), value = TRUE)
    gender_term_name <- gender_term_name[gender_term_name != "(Intercept)"]
    
    if (length(gender_term_name) > 0) {
      linear_row <- model_summary$coefficients[gender_term_name[1], ]
      results$Linear_Coefficient = linear_row["Estimate"]
      results$Linear_P_Value = linear_row["Pr(>|t|)"]
    }
    
  } else {
    formula_str <- paste(outcome, "~", predictor) 
    model <- glm(as.formula(formula_str), data = data, family = model_family)
    model_summary <- summary(model)
    
    results$R_Squared = 1 - (model$deviance / model$null.deviance)
    
    if (predictor %in% rownames(model_summary$coefficients)) {
      linear_row <- model_summary$coefficients[predictor, ]
      results$Linear_Coefficient = linear_row["Estimate"]
      results$Linear_P_Value = linear_row["Pr(>|t|)"]
    }
  }
  
  return(results)
}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# --- NEW FUNCTION: Run GAM (Smooth Term) ---
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
run_gam_regression <- function(data, predictor, outcome) {
  
  results <- list(
    Model_Type = "GAM",
    Effective_DF = NA, 
    GAM_P_Value = NA,
    R_Squared = NA
  )
  
  if (predictor == "gender") {
    formula_str <- paste(outcome, "~", predictor)
    model <- gam(as.formula(formula_str), data = data, family = gaussian)
    model_summary <- summary(model)
    
    results$R_Squared <- model_summary$r.sq 
    
    gender_term_name <- grep(paste0("^", predictor), rownames(model_summary$p.table), value = TRUE)
    gender_term_name <- gender_term_name[gender_term_name != "(Intercept)"]
    
    if (length(gender_term_name) > 0) {
      results$GAM_P_Value = model_summary$p.table[gender_term_name[1], "Pr(>|t|)"]
      results$Effective_DF = 1 
    }
    
  } else {
    formula_str <- paste(outcome, "~ s(", predictor, ")")
    model <- gam(as.formula(formula_str), data = data, family = gaussian)
    model_summary <- summary(model)
    
    results$R_Squared <- model_summary$r.sq 
    
    smooth_term_row <- model_summary$s.table
    
    if (!is.null(smooth_term_row) && nrow(smooth_term_row) > 0) {
      results$Effective_DF = smooth_term_row[1, "edf"]
      results$GAM_P_Value = smooth_term_row[1, "p-value"]
    }
  }
  
  return(results)
}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# --- NEW FUNCTION: Visualization of Significant GLM & GAM Relationships ---
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

generate_plot <- function(bio, predictor, outcome, glm_p, gam_p, glm_rsq, gam_rsq, gam_edf, Week) {
  
  # Filter plot_data only by Bio and Week from the overall StatSS dataset
  plot_data <- StatSS %>% 
    filter(Bio == bio) %>%
    filter(week == Week)
  
  # --- 1. Check Significance ---
  is_glm_sig <- glm_p < 0.05
  is_gam_sig <- gam_p < 0.05
  
  if (!is_glm_sig) {
    warning(paste("Skipping plot:", Week, bio, predictor, outcome, "as GLM was not significant. Check filtering logic."))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  if (!(predictor %in% names(plot_data) && outcome %in% names(plot_data))) {
    warning(paste("Skipping plot:", Week, bio, predictor, outcome, "due to missing columns."))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # --- 2. Build Subtitle based on significant models ---
  subtitle_parts <- c()
  
  if (is_glm_sig) {
    subtitle_parts <- c(subtitle_parts, 
                         paste0("GLM (Linear): R²=", round(glm_rsq, 3), 
                                ", P=", round(glm_p, 4)))
  }
  
  if (is_gam_sig) {
    subtitle_parts <- c(subtitle_parts, 
                         paste0("GAM (Smooth): R²=", round(gam_rsq, 3), 
                                ", P=", round(gam_p, 4), 
                                ", EDF=", round(gam_edf, 2)))
  }
  
  plot_subtitle <- paste(subtitle_parts, collapse = " | ")
  
  # --- 3. Initialize Plot ---
  
  if (predictor == "gender") {
    # --- A. BOXPLOT (for categorical gender) ---
    
    plot_data <- plot_data %>% 
      filter(!is.na(.data[[outcome]])) %>%
      filter(.data[[predictor]] %in% c("male", "female"))
    
    plot <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = .data[[predictor]], y = .data[[outcome]])) +
      geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA, fill = "gray90", color = "gray50") +
      geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, color = "#1f77b4", size = 1.5) + 
      labs(
        title = paste0(bio, ": ", outcome, " by ", predictor, " (Group Comparison, ", Week, ")"),
        subtitle = plot_subtitle,
        x = paste(predictor, "(Biomarker:", bio, ")"),
        y = outcome
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "white"),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "white")
      )
    
    cat(paste0("  Generated Boxplot for: ", Week, " ", bio, " (", predictor, ")\n"))
    
  } else {
    # --- B. SCATTER PLOT (for continuous predictors: age, BMI) ---
    
    plot <- ggplot(plot_data, aes(x = .data[[predictor]], y = .data[[outcome]])) +
      geom_point(alpha = 0.6, color = "#1f77b4") + 
      labs(
        title = paste0(bio, ": ", outcome, " ~ ", predictor, " (GLM vs GAM Fit, ", Week, ")"),
        subtitle = plot_subtitle,
        x = paste(predictor, "(Biomarker:", bio, ")"),
        y = outcome
      ) +
      theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
      theme(
        plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
        panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "white"),
        plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "white")
      )
    
    # --- 4. Conditionally Add GLM Linear Fit (Solid Blue Line) ---
    if (is_glm_sig) {
      plot <- plot + 
        geom_smooth(
          method = "lm", 
          formula = y ~ x, 
          color = "#1f77b4", 
          linetype = "solid",
          linewidth = 1.2,
          se = TRUE 
        )
      cat(paste0("  Added GLM Linear fit for: ", Week, " ", bio, " (", predictor, ")\n"))
    }
    
    # --- 5. Conditionally Add GAM Smooth Fit (Dashed Red Line) ---
    if (is_gam_sig) {
      plot <- plot +
        geom_smooth(
          method = "gam", 
          formula = y ~ s(x), 
          color = "#d62728", 
          linetype = "dashed",
          linewidth = 1.2,
          se = TRUE
        )
      cat(paste0("  Added GAM Smooth fit for: ", Week, " ", bio, " (", predictor, ")\n"))
    }
    
  }
  
  # --- 6. Save Plot to PNG File ---
  # Path structure: valid_path/Stats/Pics/{Week}/{bio}_{predictor}_vs_{outcome}.png
  file_name <- paste0(bio, "_", predictor, "_vs_", outcome, ".png")
  
  # Create the output directory including the Week level
  output_dir <- file.path(valid_path, "Stats/Pics", Week)
  if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) {
    dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
  }
  
  output_path <- file.path(output_dir, file_name)
  
  # Save the plot
  ggsave(filename = output_path, plot = plot, width = 7, height = 5, units = "in")
  cat(paste0("  Saved plot to: ", output_path, "\n"))
  
  return(plot) 
}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# --- MAIN FUNCTION: Encapsulate Analysis by Week ---
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

run_analysis_by_week <- function(current_week) {
  
  cat(paste0("\n*** Starting Analysis for Week: ", current_week, " ***\n"))
  
  # Filter data for the current week level
  CurrentStatSS <- StatSS %>%
    filter(week == current_week) %>%
    # Ensure gender is a factor for this subset
    mutate(gender = as.factor(gender))
  
  # Skip if no data
  if (nrow(CurrentStatSS) == 0) {
    warning(paste("No data found for week:", current_week, ". Skipping analysis."))
    return(NULL)
  }
  
  # --- ANALYSIS STREAMS: Execute GLM and GAM Separately ---
  
  # 1. GLM Stream (Linear)
  GLM_RegressionResults <- CurrentStatSS %>%
    group_by(Bio) %>%
    summarise(
      Combinations = list(regression_combinations),
      .groups = 'drop'
    ) %>%
    left_join(CurrentStatSS %>%
                group_by(Bio) %>%
                nest() %>%
                rename(Data = data),
              by = "Bio") %>%
    unnest(Combinations) %>%
    mutate(
      Model_Output = pmap(list(Data, Predictor, Outcome), run_glm_regression)
    ) %>%
    unnest_wider(Model_Output)
  
  # 2. GAM Stream (Smooth Terms)
  GAM_RegressionResults <- CurrentStatSS %>%
    group_by(Bio) %>%
    summarise(
      Combinations = list(regression_combinations),
      .groups = 'drop'
    ) %>%
    left_join(CurrentStatSS %>%
                group_by(Bio) %>%
                nest() %>%
                rename(Data = data),
              by = "Bio") %>%
    unnest(Combinations) %>%
    mutate(
      Model_Output = pmap(list(Data, Predictor, Outcome), run_gam_regression)
    ) %>%
    unnest_wider(Model_Output) %>%
    rename(Model_P_Value = GAM_P_Value)
  
  
  # --- Output and Filtering: Creating Wide Format ---
  
  # 1. Prepare GLM results for merge (rename columns)
  GLM_Wide <- GLM_RegressionResults %>%
    select(Bio, Predictor, Outcome, Linear_Coefficient, Linear_P_Value, R_Squared) %>%
    rename(
      GLM_Coefficient = Linear_Coefficient,
      GLM_P_Value = Linear_P_Value,
      GLM_R_Squared = R_Squared
    )
  
  # 2. Prepare GAM results for merge (rename columns)
  GAM_Wide <- GAM_RegressionResults %>%
    select(Bio, Predictor, Outcome, Model_P_Value, Effective_DF, R_Squared) %>%
    rename(
      GAM_P_Value = Model_P_Value,
      GAM_EDF = Effective_DF,
      GAM_R_Squared = R_Squared
    )
  
  # 3. Combine All Results into AgingA (Wide Format)
  AgingA_Week <- full_join(GLM_Wide, GAM_Wide, by = c("Bio", "Predictor", "Outcome")) %>%
    mutate(Week = current_week) # Add Week identifier
  
  # 4. Filter Significant Results (P < 0.05) into Aging
  Aging_Week <- AgingA_Week %>%
    filter(GLM_P_Value < 0.05) %>%
    mutate(Week = current_week) # Add Week identifier
  
  
  # --- 5. Visualization of Significant GLM & GAM Relationships ---
  if (nrow(Aging_Week) > 0) {
    cat(paste0("\nGenerating and saving ", nrow(Aging_Week), " plots for GLM-significant relationships in ", current_week, "...\n"))
    
    saved_plots <- pmap(
      list(Aging_Week$Bio, Aging_Week$Predictor, Aging_Week$Outcome,
           Aging_Week$GLM_P_Value, Aging_Week$GAM_P_Value, 
           Aging_Week$GLM_R_Squared, Aging_Week$GAM_R_Squared, Aging_Week$GAM_EDF,
           Aging_Week$Week), # Pass Week level
      generate_plot
    )
    
    # Filter out NULL results and display plots
    plots_to_print <- saved_plots[!sapply(saved_plots, is.null)]
    invisible(lapply(plots_to_print, print)) 
    
    cat(paste0(length(plots_to_print), " plots successfully saved and displayed for ", current_week, ".\n"))
  } else {
    cat(paste0("No significant GLM relationships found for ", current_week, ". No plots generated.\n"))
  }
  
  # --- 6. Export Single Week Results (Optional but good for archives) ---
  
  # For the user, we will only return the dataframes to be combined into Master,
  # but here is where you would export individual week files if needed.
  
  # Returning a list of the dataframes with a Type column for easy combining
  return(list(
    AgingA = AgingA_Week %>% mutate(Type = "AgingA"),
    Aging = Aging_Week %>% mutate(Type = "Aging")
  ))
}


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# --- RUN ALL WEEKS AND COMBINE ---
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# StatSS (full data) is used across all functions for filtering
StatSS <- Stat
StatSS$gender <- as.factor(StatSS$gender)
StatSS$week <- as.factor(StatSS$week)


# Identify the levels to loop over
week_levels <- unique(StatSS$week)
# Remove potential NA values from the week levels list if they exist
week_levels <- week_levels[!is.na(week_levels)]


# Run the analysis for all week levels and collect results
MasterResultsList <- purrr::map(week_levels, run_analysis_by_week)


# Combine all results into final master dataframes
# map_dfr is used to combine the elements (AgingA and Aging) from each list item
AgingAMaster <- MasterResultsList %>% 
  purrr::map("AgingA") %>% 
  purrr::list_rbind() %>%
  select(-Type)
  
AgingMaster <- MasterResultsList %>%
  purrr::map("Aging") %>%
  purrr::list_rbind() %>%
  select(-Type)


# Final Outputs (Printed to RStudio Console)
print("--- FINAL MASTER: ALL Combined GLM & GAM Results (AgingAMaster) ---")
print(AgingAMaster)

print("--- FINAL MASTER: Significant GLM Relationships (AgingMaster) ---")
print(AgingMaster)


# ----------------------------------------------------------------------
# --- 7. Export Master Results ---
# ----------------------------------------------------------------------

# --- Export Master Processed Data ---
export_list_master <- list(
  Aging = AgingMaster,
  AgingA = AgingAMaster
)

# Ensure the Stats directory exists for main exports
if (!dir.exists(file.path(valid_path, "Stats"))) {
  dir.create(file.path(valid_path, "Stats"), recursive = TRUE)
}

# Exporting the combined master dataframes to separate files
for (file_name in names(export_list_master)) {
  path <- file.path(valid_path, "Stats", paste0(file_name, ".xlsx"))
  write.xlsx(export_list_master[[file_name]], path, rowNames = FALSE)
  cat(paste0("Exported master file to: ", path, "\n"))
}


# Clean up
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), CoreDatasets))
```

```{r}
# --- 4. Save the Plot to specified path ---
output_dir <- file.path(valid_path, "Stats/PubPics")

# Ensure the output directory exists
if (!dir.exists(output_dir)) {
  dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)
}

file_name <- "CBT_Amplitude_vs_Age_Pub_v1.png"
output_path <- file.path(output_dir, file_name)

ggsave(filename = output_path, plot = amp_plot, width = 7, height = 7, units = "in", dpi = 300)

cat(paste0("\nSaved Publication Plot to: ", output_path, "\n"))


# Clean up
rm(list = setdiff(ls(), CoreDatasets))
```




```{r}
# ==============================================================================
# DATA SETUP AND INITIALIZATION
# (Assuming SJL data frame exists with columns: week, bio, amplitude, gender)
# ==============================================================================

# Define the list of biological variables to iterate over
biolist <- c("HR", "Steps", "Energy", "Breath", "HRV", "RR", "Cortisol", "Stress", "SBT", "CBT")

# Initialize an empty data frame to store the results of all tests
GenderStats <- data.frame()

cat("\n--- Running Batch T-Tests and Power Analyses ---\n")

# ==============================================================================
# 1. LOOP THROUGH BIOLIST FOR T-TESTS AND POWER ANALYSIS
# ==============================================================================

for (current_bio in biolist) {
  cat(paste("\nAnalyzing:", current_bio, "...\n"))

  # A. Filter the data for the current bio-metric and for 'week == Both'
  # We assume 'amplitude' is the dependent variable for all 'bio' types
  SJL_filtered <- SJL %>%
    filter(week == "Both", bio == current_bio) %>%
    # Ensure only rows with non-NA values for both variables are considered
    drop_na(amplitude, gender)

  # Check if there is enough data in both groups to perform a test
  n_female <- SJL_filtered %>% filter(gender == "female") %>% nrow()
  n_male <- SJL_filtered %>% filter(gender == "male") %>% nrow()

  if (n_female < 2 | n_male < 2) {
    cat(paste("Skipping", current_bio, ": Insufficient data (N_F =", n_female, ", N_M =", n_male, ") for t-test.\n"))
    # Add a row of NAs to maintain structure in GenderStats for skipped tests
    new_row <- data.frame(
      bio = current_bio,
      t_value = NA, df = NA, p_value = NA, cohens_d = NA,
      n_female = n_female, n_male = n_male, power = NA
    )
    GenderStats <- rbind(GenderStats, new_row)
    next
  }

  # B. Independent Samples T-Test
  t_result <- t.test(amplitude ~ gender, data = SJL_filtered, var.equal = TRUE) # Assuming equal variance for simplicity/consistency

  # C. Effect Size (Cohen's d)
  d_result <- SJL_filtered %>%
    cohens_d(amplitude ~ gender, var.equal = TRUE)
  cohens_d_value <- d_result$effsize[1]

  # D. Power Analysis
  n_avg <- mean(c(n_female, n_male))
  power_result <- pwr.t.test(
    n = n_avg,
    d = cohens_d_value,
    sig.level = 0.05,
    type = "two.sample",
    alternative = "two.sided",
    power = NULL
  )

  # E. Compile and Append Results
  new_row <- data.frame(
    bio = current_bio,
    t_value = t_result$statistic,
    df = t_result$parameter,
    p_value = t_result$p.value,
    cohens_d = cohens_d_value,
    n_female = n_female,
    n_male = n_male,
    power = power_result$power
  )

  GenderStats <- rbind(GenderStats, new_row)
  cat(paste("Results saved (p =", round(t_result$p.value, 4), ")\n"))
}

# ==============================================================================
# 2. DISPLAY SUMMARY TABLE
# ==============================================================================
cat("\n--- Final GenderStats Summary Table ---\n")
print(GenderStats %>%
        # Add a significance indicator column for easier reading
        mutate(Significance = ifelse(p_value < 0.05, "YES", "NO")) %>%
        select(bio, p_value, cohens_d, power, Significance, n_female, n_male) %>%
        # Round numerical columns for display
        mutate(across(c(p_value, cohens_d, power), ~round(., 4)))
)

# ==============================================================================
# 3. COMBINED BOXPLOT VISUALIZATION (STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT ONLY)
# ==============================================================================

# Filter for significant results (p < 0.05)
significant_bios <- GenderStats %>%
  filter(p_value < 0.05) %>%
  pull(bio)

# Filter the main data (SJL) to include only the significant 'bio' types
SJL_sig_plot_data <- SJL %>%
  filter(week == "Both", bio %in% significant_bios) %>%
  filter(!is.na(gender), !is.na(amplitude))

cat("\n--- Generating Combined Boxplot for Significant Comparisons ---\n")

if (length(significant_bios) > 0) {
  # Create the combined plot using facet_wrap
  combined_plot <- SJL_sig_plot_data %>%
    ggplot(aes(x = gender, y = amplitude, fill = gender, color = gender)) +
    
    # Boxplot uses the 'fill' aesthetic. Use black for border for definition.
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, outlier.shape = NA, color = "black") +
    
    # Jitter points use the 'color' aesthetic.
    geom_jitter(width = 0.2, alpha = 0.6, size = 1.5) +
    
    # Define manual fill colors for the boxes (Light Red and Light Blue)
    scale_fill_manual(values = c("female" = "#FAD0D0", "male" = "#D0D0FA")) +
    
    # Define manual color for the jitter points (Red and Blue)
    scale_color_manual(values = c("female" = "#E41A1C", "male" = "#377EB8")) +
    
    labs(
      title = "Amplitude Differences by Gender (Only p < 0.05 Shown)",
      subtitle = paste0("Total Significant Metrics: ", length(significant_bios)),
      x = "Gender",
      y = "Amplitude"
    ) +
    
    # Split the graph by the significant 'bio' type
    # 'scales = "free_y"' allows the y-axis scale to adjust for each metric
    facet_wrap(~ bio, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
    
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
      panel.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "white"),
      plot.background = element_rect(fill = "white", colour = "white"),
      legend.position = "none",
      strip.background = element_rect(fill = "#E0E0E0", color = "black"),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold")
    )
  
  print(combined_plot)
} else {
  cat("No statistically significant comparisons (p < 0.05) found to plot.\n")
}

# The final GenderStats data frame containing all results is now available in the R environment.
```
